warnings: Respiratory depression (especially with concurrent opioids)
Rare paradoxical agitation

indications.label: IM (status epilepticus)
indications.notes: RAMPART trial: IM midaz ≥ IV lorazepam in efficacy

indications.label: Procedural sedation (IV)
indications.frequency: Slow IV push, may repeat after 2-3 min

indications.label: Intranasal (anxiolysis/seizure)
indications.notes: Use 5 mg/mL concentration, split between both nostrils; usable in the field for seizures

clinical.contraindications: Myasthenia gravis, acute angle-closure glaucoma, respiratory failure
clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression (especially with opioids), drowsiness, rare paradoxical agitation
clinical.warnings: Have flumazenil ready; IM/IN is a good field option for neonatal seizures (RAMPART)

lorazepam_inj.notes: Quick note: 20 kg = one ampoule (2 mg); first-line for status epilepticus
lorazepam_inj.frequency: Slow IV push (over 2-5 min), may repeat after 5-10 min

clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression, drowsiness, rare paradoxical agitation
clinical.warnings: Slow IV push over 2-5 min; have flumazenil ready; max 4 mg/dose

diazepam_iv.notes: Status epilepticus alternative agent (first choice is lorazepam)
diazepam_iv.frequency: Slow IV push (over 2-3 min), may repeat after 5 min

clinical.use: Status epilepticus second-line, anxiolysis, muscle spasm
clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression, drowsiness, phlebitis (IV)
clinical.warnings: Slow IV push over 2-3 min; max 10 mg/dose; lorazepam remains first-line

diazepam_pr.notes: Commonly used for prehospital/home febrile seizures; convenient when no IV access. Clinically often dosed by number of tubes (one tube = 10 mg); mL conversion is for reference
diazepam_pr.frequency: ST, may repeat once after 5-10 min
diazepam_pr.concentration_note: 5 mg/2.5 mL/tube or 10 mg/2.5 mL/tube (selected by age)

clinical.use: Prehospital/home febrile seizures, status epilepticus (no IV access)
clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression, drowsiness
clinical.warnings: 0.5 mg/kg PR; max 20 mg/dose; may give again after 5-10 min

keppra_syrup.notes: For children or those unable to swallow tablets

clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, agitation, behavioral change (children)
clinical.warnings: Initial 20 mg/kg/day → titrate to 40-60 mg/kg/day; BID

keppra_tab.notes: For acute status, use IV loading; after ROSC or for outpatient maintenance, switch to oral. Initial 20 mg/kg/day → titrate to 40-60 mg/kg/day based on seizure control

clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, agitation
clinical.warnings: Max 3000 mg/day; adjust dose in renal impairment

keppra_iv.notes: ESETT 2019: 60 mg/kg over 10 min, efficacy comparable to fosphenytoin and valproate; dilute 1 vial (500 mg) to 50-100 mL N/S

clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, agitation, rare psychiatric symptoms (aggression / depression)
clinical.warnings: ESETT 2019: 60 mg/kg over 10 min; reduce dose in renal impairment

depakine_syrup.notes: Initial 10-15 mg/kg/day → titrate based on seizure control; target serum level 50-100 µg/mL
depakine_syrup.frequency: BID (maintenance dose; may titrate up to 60 mg/kg/day)
warnings: Contraindicated in liver disease and mitochondrial disease
POMC encephalopathy

clinical.contraindications: Liver disease, mitochondrial disease, urea cycle disorder
clinical.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity, weight gain (↑), tremor, hair loss
clinical.warnings: Monitor LFT, CBC; target serum level 50-100 µg/mL; hepatotoxicity risk higher when age < 2 years

depakine_tab.notes: ≥ 30 kg suitable for tablets; < 30 kg use syrup
warnings: Contraindicated in liver disease and mitochondrial disease

clinical.contraindications: Liver disease, mitochondrial disease, urea cycle disorder
clinical.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity, weight gain (↑), tremor
clinical.warnings: ≥30 kg suitable for tablets; hepatotoxicity risk higher when age < 2 years

depakine_iv.notes: ESETT 2019: 40 mg/kg over 10 min; dilute 1 vial (400 mg) to 50 mL N/S; rate 1.5-3 mg/kg/min
warnings: Contraindicated in liver disease and mitochondrial disease
POMC encephalopathy

clinical.contraindications: Liver disease, mitochondrial disease, urea cycle disorder, pregnancy
clinical.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, decreased platelets (↓), hyperammonemia
clinical.warnings: ESETT 2019: 40 mg/kg over 10 min; rate 1.5-3 mg/kg/min

phenobarbital_iv.notes: SE loading dose; IV rate ≤ 30 mg/min (children ≤ 1 mg/kg/min); respiratory depression more likely if given after BZD

clinical.use: Status Epilepticus first-line alternative (when no BZD available) / second-line (when other ASMs unavailable); first choice for neonatal seizure
clinical.contraindications: Severe hepatic insufficiency, acute intermittent porphyria, barbiturate hypersensitivity
clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression (especially with concurrent BZD), hypotension, excessive sedation, behavioral change
clinical.warnings: Give slow IV ≤ 30 mg/min; have intubation/vasopressor ready; neonatal dose 20 mg/kg
clinical.breastfeeding: May pass into breast milk, drowsiness — short-term use acceptable, evaluate for long-term use

phenytoin_iv.notes: SE loading (substitute for fosphenytoin when unavailable in-house); IV rate ≤ 1 mg/kg/min (children max 50 mg/min); dilute with NS (D5W will precipitate); administer through a filter

clinical.use: Status Epilepticus second-line; epilepsy long-term control
clinical.contraindications: Sinus bradycardia, SA block, AV block, Adams-Stokes syndrome, hydantoin hypersensitivity
clinical.adverseEffects: Arrhythmia, hypotension, purple glove syndrome (extravasation), Stevens-Johnson syndrome, gingival hyperplasia (long-term)
clinical.warnings: Monitor ECG + BP; dilute with NS, do not use D5W (will precipitate); use in-line filter; extravasation → purple glove syndrome can cause tissue necrosis
clinical.pregnancy: AU TGA: D (teratogenic — fetal hydantoin syndrome)
clinical.breastfeeding: Small amounts pass into breast milk; breastfeeding is generally acceptable

ketamine.monitoring: SpO2, ETCO2, HR, BP; have O2, Ambu bag, suction, atropine, midazolam ready
warnings: Side effects: BP↑, ICP↑, IOP↑, arrhythmias, apnea, laryngospasm, delirium, N/V, nystagmus
Barbiturates and ketamine must not share a syringe (will precipitate)
Traditional teaching of increased ICP has been challenged by recent literature (safe in most TBI patients)
Hypersalivation — pre-treatment with atropine 0.01 mg/kg is no longer routine (ACEP 2011)
Emergence reactions — give midazolam 0.05 mg/kg beforehand; higher risk in school-age children
Contraindications: <3 months (laryngospasm risk), active psychosis, uncontrolled HTN, thyrotoxicosis, global eyeball injury

contraindications.reason: High laryngospasm risk when age < 3 months

indications.label: IM (induction / procedural sedation)
indications.notes: Anesthesia induction 4-6 mg/kg; procedural sedation 4-5 mg/kg
indications.frequency: ST × 1 (induction); for procedural sedation, may repeat 2-5 mg/kg after 5-10 min if needed

indications.label: IV (induction / procedural sedation)
indications.notes: Induction 0.5-2 mg/kg; procedural sedation 1-2 mg/kg. Hemodynamically stable, suitable for hypotension/shock
indications.frequency: Slow push 30-60 sec; for procedural sedation, repeat 0.5-1 mg/kg q5-10 min if needed

indications.label: IV maintenance (anesthesia)
indications.notes: General anesthesia maintenance (used in OR, less common in ED)
indications.frequency: Bolus followed by continuous infusion up to 1 mg/kg/hr

indications.label: IV sub-dissociative analgesia
indications.notes: Acute pain, opioid-sparing; may give as IV drip 0.1-0.3 mg/kg/hr
indications.frequency: Slow IV over 10 min; may repeat q15-30 min

clinical.use: Procedural sedation, RSI induction, acute pain sub-dissociative dosing
clinical.contraindications: <3 months, active psychosis, uncontrolled HTN, global eyeball injury, thyrotoxicosis
clinical.adverseEffects: BP↑, ICP↑, IOP↑, laryngospasm (rare ~0.4%), emergence reaction, N/V, nystagmus, hypersalivation
clinical.warnings: Barbiturates must not share a syringe (precipitate); have atropine + midazolam ready for emergence reactions; hemodynamically stable, suitable for hypotension/shock

citosol.notes: Sedation for imaging studies (CT/MRI); may repeat until asleep; total volume should not exceed the patient's weight in mL
citosol.concentration_note: 0.5 amp + N/S to 20 mL; start at 1/3-1/4 of body weight in mL
warnings: Respiratory depression
Hypotension

clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression, hypotension, myocardial depression
clinical.warnings: Slow IV titrate; have airway equipment ready; reduce dose in the elderly / heart failure

chloral_hydrate.notes: Procedural sedation (imaging, EEG, AS); onset 30-60 min, duration 1-2 hr. 10% solution = 100 mg/mL, so 0.5 mL/kg = 50 mg/kg
chloral_hydrate.frequency: ST, may repeat after 30 min if needed
warnings: Respiratory depression
Arrhythmia (high dose)
Older guidelines capped at 50 mg/kg; newer Lexicomp accepts 25-100 mg/kg/dose

clinical.adverseEffects: Respiratory depression (high dose), GI upset, rare arrhythmia
clinical.warnings: Discontinued in Europe/US in recent years due to safety concerns; max 100 mg/kg or 2 g per procedure

vena_tab.notes: Oral for allergy/sedation; max 5 mg/kg/day or 300 mg/day
warnings: Use with caution under 3 years of age

clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth
clinical.warnings: Use with caution <3 years; max 5 mg/kg/day or 300 mg/day

vena_inj.notes: First-line for allergic reaction; often combined with metoclopramide to prevent EPS

clinical.use: Acute allergic reaction, anaphylaxis adjunct, EPS reversal
clinical.adverseEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, urinary retention, rare paradoxical agitation
clinical.warnings: Epinephrine remains primary treatment for anaphylaxis; for EPS use 1-2 mg/kg IV

epinephrine_arrest.notes: Cardiac arrest / severe bradycardia; mL volume = 0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL (1:10000). Follow push with a 5 mL N/S flush
epinephrine_arrest.concentration_note: Arrest dosing uses 0.1 mg/mL = 1:10000 (dilute 1 amp of 1 mg/mL stock × with 9 mL N/S to make 10 mL)
warnings: Do not push through the same IV line as NaHCO3 (will inactivate)

clinical.use: Cardiac arrest, anaphylaxis, severe bradycardia, croup (IH)
clinical.adverseEffects: Increased heart rate (↑), HTN, tremor, pulmonary edema (overdose)
clinical.warnings: Arrest dosing uses 1:10000 (0.1 mg/mL) IV/IO 0.01 mg/kg; do not share an IV line with NaHCO3 (inactivate)

amiodarone_arrest.notes: Refractory VF/pVT; give as rapid push during arrest; for non-arrest wide-QRS tachycardia, give IV over 20-60 min
amiodarone_arrest.frequency: Bolus during arrest, may repeat up to 3 times (subsequent doses max 150 mg/dose)
warnings: Do not give as rapid push outside of arrest (hypotension)

clinical.contraindications: Severe sinus bradycardia, SA/AV block (without pacemaker), iodine hypersensitivity
clinical.adverseEffects: Hypotension (rapid push), QT prolongation, pulmonary fibrosis (long-term), liver/thyroid abnormality
clinical.warnings: May give as rapid push during arrest; outside arrest give IV over 20-60 min; max 300 mg first dose, 150 mg subsequent

lidocaine_arrest.notes: Amiodarone alternative; one of the second-line options for refractory VF/pVT
lidocaine_arrest.frequency: Bolus during arrest; maintenance 20-50 mcg/kg/min after ROSC

clinical.adverseEffects: CNS effects (drowsiness, seizure at high dose), bradycardia, low BP
clinical.warnings: Bolus 1 mg/kg; maintenance 20-50 µg/kg/min after ROSC; max total 3 mg/kg

atropine_brady.notes: Used for symptomatic bradycardia caused by increased vagal tone or primary AV block. For general bradycardia, epinephrine remains first choice. Min dose 0.1 mg (avoid paradoxical bradycardia)
atropine_brady.frequency: May repeat 1 time (single dose max 0.5 mg)
warnings: Min 0.1 mg, otherwise may paradoxically slow the heart rate further

clinical.use: Symptomatic bradycardia (vagal tone↑ or primary AV block), organophosphate poisoning
clinical.adverseEffects: Dry mouth, blurred vision, increased heart rate (↑), urinary retention
clinical.warnings: Min 0.1 mg (avoid paradoxical bradycardia); max 0.5 mg single dose; may repeat 1 time

warnings: Note: transient asystole / heart block is an expected response (half-life <10 seconds)
May trigger bronchospasm in asthma patients

indications.label: 1st dose (SVT)
indications.notes: Use the closest IV line (the closer to the heart, the better); print rhythm strip after administration
indications.frequency: Rapid push + immediate 5-10 mL N/S flush (use a stopcock to push with two syringes simultaneously)

indications.label: 2nd dose (if no response in 1-2 min)
indications.notes: May repeat once more (max single dose 12 mg)

clinical.contraindications: 2nd/3rd degree AV block (without pacemaker), sick sinus syndrome, severe asthma
clinical.adverseEffects: Transient asystole / heart block (expected response), flushing, chest tightness, rare bronchospasm
clinical.warnings: Rapid push + immediate flush (use a stopcock with two syringes, or the closest IV line); half-life <10 sec; turn on ECG recording before administration
